top.description: Simsbury football coach Jim Caouette talks with Hunter Woolf during a 27-7 win over Newington at Holden Field in Simsbury on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. (Bryant Carpenter/Hearst Connecticut Media) SIMSBURY - The leaves are off the trees beyond the north end zone of Holden Field, but the Simsbury Trojans who play there remain at peak. With a 27-7 win over Newington on Friday night, Simsbury football improved to 7-1. Which means the town that is home to the Pinchot Sycamore, the state's biggest tree, is home to the team enjoying the season's biggest turnaround in Connecticut high school football . Mark the rings on the trunk: Simsbury was 1-9 a year ago, 2-8 in 2024 and 1-9 in 2023. Heading into 2026, the team had its third head coach in as many years come through the door. He's proven to be a good one. Jim Caouette, the longtime defensive coordinator at Holy Cross-Waterbury and one-time head coach at Avon, a ball of energy and new schemes on both sides of the ball, harnessed a 19-strong group of seniors hungry to win as they once did before they got to high school. Another advantage: Simsbury moved down a rung on the Central Connecticut Conference ladder, from Tier 2 to Tier 3. There, the Trojans have not lost since dropping their season opener to Middletown, 40-35. They've won seven straight, the second-longest streak in program history, and stand No. 4 in the CIAC Class L playoff rankings. They are on course to match the 9-1 of 2019, the last time Simsbury football reached the postseason. It had been one long dry spell since, a meager 12 wins across five seasons. This fall, the Trojans pushed all that to the curb. "I think last year and years prior we've just been beating ourselves up on our own; it's been 'Simsbury versus Simsbury' is what the coaches say," remarked senior captain and lineman Brett Osborne. "So I think we've really learned how to take it in and move forward instead of taking steps backwards." The Trojans have two games remaining with E.O. Smith and Glastonbury. Their plus-6 shift in victories so far puts them ahead of several other teams of marked improvement this season. New London (3-7 to 8-0), Tolland (1-8 to 6-2) and Thames River (2-7 to 7-1) increased by five wins. Lewis Mills/Wolcott Tech (2-8 to 6-2), New Milford (1-9 to 5-3) and the SMSA Co-op (1-9 to 5-2) each improved by four wins thus far. Of note: New London and Thames River are also under new coaching regimes. Jack Cochran is back at New London after being out of the game for 13 years. Will Henton is in his first head coaching position with the Thames River co-op of Grasso and Norwich Tech. Caouette led Avon for three seasons, 2013 through 2015, and went 23-9. He is better known as the assistant coach who oversaw the Holy Cross defense for the next decade while his son Drew became the school's top all-time passer . top.title: Uranus has a weird magnetic field that's stumped scientists for 40 years — we may finally know why
top.description: The posided magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune may stem from extreme conditions lying within their deep interior. Unravelling the mystery behind the magnetic fields of these worlds is giving us new insight into the little-known interiors of the ice giants. Only one spacecraft has ever visited Uranus and Neptune, the Voyager 2 spacecraft which spend past Uranus in January 1986 and Neptune in August 1989. Voyager 2 found that their planetary magnetic fields were, to put it bluntly, wonky. Uranus’ magnetic field was offset from its rotational axis by 59 degrees and isn’t even centered on the planet’s core, but instead is only two-thirds of the way down. Neptune is similar, with a disordered magnetic field offset by 47 degrees and centered halfway between the core and its visible cloud tops. If we compare these planets to Earth , which has a stable magnetic field tilted by just 11 degrees to our planet’s rotation, we can see how extreme the magnetic fields of the ice giants are. Various explanations for the strange magnetic fields of the ice giants have been put forward over the years. Uranus as a whole is tilted by 97 degrees and effectively rolls around the sun , and speculation is that billions of years ago it was knocked on its side by a collision with a long-lost Earth-sized planet. Could this collision have also skewed its magnetic field? This might be a plausible explanation were Neptune’s magnetic field also not similarly skewed without having experienced a collision. Clearly, whatever the cause, it must be intrinsic to the nature of the two ice giant planets. Now, a new study by scientists in the U.S. and the UK, based on computer simulations and Voyager 2’s measurements of the two planets’ magnetic fields, may have found a solution. The solution to the weird magnetic fields of the solar system's ice giants may come down to how planets generate their magnetic field through the dynamo effect. This arises from the swirling, convective motion of an electrically conducting liquid within a rotating body, which is able to generate and maintain a powerful magnetic field. Inside Earth, the electrically conducting fluid is the molten iron in the outer part of our planet’s core, and the magnetic field that it generates has clear north and south poles – what we call a dipole, a phenomenon that we can also see in the two magnetic poles of a simple bar magnet. However, the conditions inside Uranus and Neptune are somewhat different. As ice giants, they contain a lot of volatiles – ammonia, hydrogen, helium, methane, and water surrounding a probable rocky core. Furthermore, Uranus and Neptune are substantially larger than Earth , with 14.5 and 17 times the mass of our planet, respectively. This increased mass creates crushing conditions within the interior of the ice giants. top.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Professor Joash Amupitan SAN, has urged members of the 2027 Election Petition Tribunals to avoid technicalities that defeat substantive justice and to subject electronic evidence to rigorous scrutiny. He also told them to keep firm control of their courtrooms and let “truth of the ballot prevail”. According to the commission’s Daily Bulletin of Tuesday, Amupitan spoke on Monday in Abuja while delivering the Commission’s opening remarks at a three-day workshop for Justices of the Court of Appeal and members of the tribunals, held at the Body of Benchers Complex. The Court of Appeal organised the workshop under the theme “Election Tribunal as a Tool for Political Stability.” The INEC chairman said electoral litigation had grown more complex, with disputes now touching on voter accreditation, electronic transmission of results, technological failures and the integrity of digital records. On the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System BVAS and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), he said technology should neither be treated as infallible nor dismissed simply because the evidence is electronic. Amupitan warned that digital disinformation driven by artificial intelligence, audio cloning and deepfake videos would inevitably spill into the courtrooms. He urged the tribunals to apply strict evidentiary standards under Section 84 of the Evidence Act, saying digital provenance, forensic chain of custody and reliance on certified data from INEC would be vital to stop synthetic fabrications from misleading the courts. He added that electoral adjudication is evidence-driven, and that allegations of irregularities, non-compliance or result manipulation must be proved with credible and legally admissible evidence. According to him, the Commission has issued the Regulations and Guidelines for the Conduct of Elections, 2026, to give clearer operational standards against which claims of non-compliance can be weighed in proceedings. The INEC chairman told the tribunal members that they carry the democratic aspirations of over 200 million Nigerians once they take their oaths. He described the courtroom as the altar on which public confidence in constitutional governance is preserved, and urged them to let their decisions reflect deep fidelity to the law, uncompromising integrity and the principle that justice must be seen to be done. Amupitan said Nigeria’s political stability in 2027 would depend not only on how efficiently INEC conducts elections, but also on how courageously, transparently and justly the tribunals settle the disputes that follow. He described the Election Petition Tribunal as a constitutional valve that releases political pressure and keeps electoral friction from degenerating into civil disruption. top.title: Stephen Jones Admits Dallas Must Learn To Close Games Now
top.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys barely survived a close battle with the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, but the victory does not mean the job is done. Stephen Jones, the team’s co-owner, made it clear that the franchise still has a key lesson to learn after the 27-23 win. The game felt eerily similar to the loss against Arizona the week before, and the team needs to fix its habit of letting leads slip away. Jones did not mince words about the state of the squad. “I think it’s something that — it’s a learning experience. I still think we’ve got a long ways to go,” Jones said. The team has to learn how to win and how to close out games, which remains a major problem for this group. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer agrees with this assessment and knows the team must do better things to succeed. Penalties Are Killing Dallas The most glaring issue on the field was a lack of discipline that nearly cost the Cowboys the game. Pro Football Network reported that Dallas’s 14 penalties totaling 153 yards erased over 100 yards of total offense. Former NFL star Chad Johnson was furious about the sloppy play and warned the team that they cannot have so many penalties if they want to win. Johnson compared the team’s behavior to the Oakland Raiders of the 80s and 90s. The worst moment came when inactive linebacker DeMarvion Overshown ran onto the field in street clothes to celebrate a big play. Referee Clay Martin called an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for the non-uniform player in blue sweats and a stocking cap. “After the play, unsportsmanlike conduct by Dallas. We had a non-uniform player in blue sweats and a stocking cap come onto the field to celebrate. That’s a 15-yard penalty,” the official announced. After a mistake shifted Dallas from its own 33-yard line to the 18, Indianapolis tied the game following a three-and-out. Closing The Game Remains A Struggle Even with a strong offensive showing, the Cowboys could not put the game away when they had the chance. Quarterback Dak Prescott called the offensive penalties “purely unacceptable” after the game, highlighting the frustration within the locker room. The team has made good plays, but drives often end up the way no one wants them to end in terms of moving the ball and scoring. “In this particular case, last week was no different closing the game out. We’re just not getting that done right now,” Jones noted regarding the struggles to finish drives. The Cowboys now sit at a 4-5 record on the season and must clean up these mistakes quickly. With the playoff race still alive, the team trails the New York Giants by just 2.5 games for first place in the NFC East. Dallas faces a tough test next as they prepare to play the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 4:25 p.m. ET at AT&T Stadium.

top.title: Real Madrid midfielder set to undergo tests after suffering injury in national team camp
top.description: Real Madrid midfielder set to undergo tests after suffering injury in national team camp The international break has just begun but it appears that disaster has already struck as far as Real Madrid are concerned. One of their key players, Aurelien Tchouameni has suffered an injury while away with the France national team, reports L’Equipe . Tchouameni injured again Tchouameni missed the start of the 2026/27 season due to an injury he had sustained with France at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. While he returned to action in September, new France manager Zinedine Zidane opted not to call him up to the squad during the previous international break, giving him time to fully recover his fitness and rhythm. Injured again? (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Since then, Tchouameni has done exactly that, once again establishing himself as an important player for Los Blancos , and earning a recall to the French national team for their upcoming UEFA Nations League matches against Italy and Turkiye. However, as per the report, Tchouameni was forced to stop training during today’s session after suffering a groin injury. Having been unable to complete the session, the 26-year-old midfielder will now undergo tests to determine the nature and severity of the injury. Once that is done, it will be decided whether Tchouameni will travel to Italy with the rest of the France squad return to the club. Concern for Real Madrid As already mentioned, Tchouameni has once again become an integral part of the Real Madrid setup under Jose Mourinho. A key cog in Mourinho’s system. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The French midfielder is key to providing the defensive solidity on the field operating alongside someone like Bernardo Silva in the double pivot. Since returning from injury, he has made ten appearances for Real Madrid in all competitions, starting eight of those, indicating the faith that Mourinho has in him. As such, if Tchouameni is injured with the France national team camp, it will come as a big blow for Los Blancos heading into an important stretch of the season. For now, those at Valdebebas will be eagerly awaiting results of the French international’s medical examinations and hoping that the groin issue he is dealing with does not turn out to be something serious.

nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Professor Joash Amupitan SAN, has urged members of the 2027 Election Petition Tribunals to avoid technicalities that defeat substantive justice and to subject electronic evidence to rigorous scrutiny. He also told them to keep firm control of their courtrooms and let “truth of the ballot prevail”. According to the commission’s Daily Bulletin of Tuesday, Amupitan spoke on Monday in Abuja while delivering the Commission’s opening remarks at a three-day workshop for Justices of the Court of Appeal and members of the tribunals, held at the Body of Benchers Complex. The Court of Appeal organised the workshop under the theme “Election Tribunal as a Tool for Political Stability.” The INEC chairman said electoral litigation had grown more complex, with disputes now touching on voter accreditation, electronic transmission of results, technological failures and the integrity of digital records. On the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System BVAS and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), he said technology should neither be treated as infallible nor dismissed simply because the evidence is electronic. Amupitan warned that digital disinformation driven by artificial intelligence, audio cloning and deepfake videos would inevitably spill into the courtrooms. He urged the tribunals to apply strict evidentiary standards under Section 84 of the Evidence Act, saying digital provenance, forensic chain of custody and reliance on certified data from INEC would be vital to stop synthetic fabrications from misleading the courts. He added that electoral adjudication is evidence-driven, and that allegations of irregularities, non-compliance or result manipulation must be proved with credible and legally admissible evidence. According to him, the Commission has issued the Regulations and Guidelines for the Conduct of Elections, 2026, to give clearer operational standards against which claims of non-compliance can be weighed in proceedings. The INEC chairman told the tribunal members that they carry the democratic aspirations of over 200 million Nigerians once they take their oaths. He described the courtroom as the altar on which public confidence in constitutional governance is preserved, and urged them to let their decisions reflect deep fidelity to the law, uncompromising integrity and the principle that justice must be seen to be done. Amupitan said Nigeria’s political stability in 2027 would depend not only on how efficiently INEC conducts elections, but also on how courageously, transparently and justly the tribunals settle the disputes that follow. The meeting was held ahead of the formal signing of the agreement, according to a statement by the Ministry’s Head of Press and Public Relations, Mrs Mary Ali. Tunji-Ojo said the automation and the integration of identity databases would help the authorities verify the nationality of people being returned to Nigeria more quickly and accurately. He identified three categories of people who may be subject to readmission: those holding valid Nigerian travel documents, those who travelled with documents but later lost or destroyed them, and those who travelled without any identification. He said the government was developing systems to establish the identities of such persons through available national records. The minister added that similar arrangements were already being implemented with the United Kingdom, while discussions were ongoing with the United States to replicate the system. He described the agreement as significant, both for facilitating the return of Nigerians with no legal grounds to remain in EU member states and for promoting a more orderly, dignified and mutually beneficial migration management system. Tunji-Ojo assured the EU delegation that Nigeria would honour every provision of the agreement. He stressed that the government’s position on irregular migration was clear, saying Nigeria does not encourage illegal migration or any abuse of the trust established between countries. According to him, building mutual trust should come before discussions on easing migration procedures, since greater confidence between Nigeria and its international partners would create better conditions for legal migration and cooperation. On border security, the minister called for stronger international collaboration and real-time information sharing, particularly against human trafficking, migrant smuggling and other cross-border crimes. Anthropic had been expected to raise up to $100 billion in its IPO, which would have made it the largest IPO on record. The stock market debut is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last. And it comes as Wall Street is busy digesting the impact of the US midterm elections, in which Democrats won majority control of both chambers of Congress and are vowing to put the brakes on President Donald Trump’s agenda. Growth has been staggering at the company. Anthropic’s revenue reached $17 billion in the third quarter, up from just $1.4 billion a year earlier, a securities filing showed earlier this month. On Tuesday, the company said its annualized projection, known as the run-rate revenue, “was approximately $81 billion as of October 31, 2026, up $10 billion from September 30.” Estimates in recent months had forecast Anthropic’s valuation at up to a staggering $2 trillion, but the estimates have slipped along with a slide in AI stock prices on Wall Street. For businesses, content creators, and people researching social media trends, another question can be just as interesting: which accounts does that person choose to follow? Someone may publicly promote fashion, technology, or entertainment while following creators in entirely different fields. A business account may begin following emerging influencers long before announcing a collaboration. A public figure may gradually change the types of accounts appearing on their Following list. The results can support social media research, although they cannot explain why someone followed an account or reveal information that Instagram keeps private. Why Follower Counts Don’t Tell the Whole Story Follower numbers are among Instagram’s most visible statistics. They influence how people assess popularity, reach, and sometimes commercial value. Yet having a large audience doesn’t necessarily mean an account has a clearly defined set of interests or strong connections within a particular industry. The Following list offers a different perspective. Consider a technology commentator who starts following several artificial intelligence researchers, software companies, and digital policy organizations. Those additions may suggest topics worth investigating. Similarly, a lifestyle influencer who follows numerous local restaurants might be exploring a new content category. Neither example proves a professional plan or future collaboration. Following someone can reflect curiosity, personal connections, or temporary interest. Still, when researchers compare several observations across time, they may discover changes worth examining further. A following tracker focuses on changes within those 600 connections, not on identifying people who recently followed the creator. Their profiles may feature carefully selected photographs, polished videos, and short biographies, but their everyday interactions with content can tell another story. A person who rarely posts about travel may regularly like photographs of unfamiliar destinations. A creator known for fashion might engage with technology tutorials, food videos, or sports content. These interactions can suggest topics that attract someone’s attention, even when they don’t appear on the person’s own profile. Someone might like a photograph because they admire the subject, appreciate the photography, support a friend, or agree with a message. For content creators and marketers, likes also form part of the wider picture of audience engagement. A beauty influencer may notice that certain makeup tutorials attract more engagement than product announcements. A restaurant could discover that behind-the-scenes videos generate stronger reactions than ordinary menu photographs. These observations can guide content decisions, especially when combined with comments, shares, reach, and other performance metrics. But there is an important difference between analyzing engagement on your own posts and studying what a particular public account likes elsewhere. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Warns iOS Flaw Could Expose Wallet Seed Phrases as Apple’s Latest iPhone Patch Stays Silent Binance warned iPhone users Tuesday that a publicly released iOS flaw could let malicious apps read files stored by other apps, including the seed phrases and private keys that control crypto wallets. “A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem,” the exchange wrote on X. “This is an iOS-level issue, not unique to Binance.” Binance told users to delete any apps installed from untrusted sources, such as sideloaded or manually signed IPA files, and to update iOS and every app to the latest official versions. Anyone who suspects a breach should move funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and reset all active login sessions, the exchange said. Neither Binance nor the researcher behind the flaw has reported any thefts tied to it. What worse_query does The bug is a sandbox escape. On iOS, each app is supposed to live in its own container that other apps cannot read. A researcher who posts as forcequitOS released worse_query on GitHub on Nov. 8, calling it “a zero-day sandbox escape for iOS 26 and 27, again.” It succeeds an earlier exploit, bad_query. The project’s README says it works on iOS 26.0 through 26.7.2 and on iOS 27.2, a wider range than the versions Binance named. It lists paths it can reach, including other apps’ data containers and shared app group folders. The researcher describes it as “a proof-of-concept for developers” that “isn’t useful by itself,” and stresses it is not a jailbreak. To use it, a developer has to build it into an app. That has already happened in at least one case. A day after the release, developer Christoph Kolbicz published a file manager built on worse_query that lets users browse and edit app data on iOS 27 without jailbreaking, which he said was tested on iOS 27.0.1. Blockchain security firm SlowMist called worse_query a container sandbox escape rather than a jailbreak. Its chief information security officer, who posts as 23pds, wrote that the flaw will not steal assets on its own. The risk comes when a user installs and runs an untrusted IPA that then reads other apps’ containers, and only if a wallet stores mnemonic phrases, keystores or WebView caches in plain text on the device. Apple’s iOS updates don’t mention it Apple shipped iOS 27.2.1 and iOS 26.7.3 on Nov. 9, a day after the proof of concept went public. Their security notes list fixes for AirPlay, Bluetooth pairing, brotli and other components, but neither names worse_query or describes a sandbox escape of this kind. That leaves it unclear whether the latest iOS builds block the technique. The exposure depends heavily on how each wallet app stores secrets. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Miami-Dade County Now Accepts Bitcoin for Property Taxes Miami-Dade County Tax Collector Dariel Fernandez said Monday his office has begun accepting bitcoin for property tax payments, both online and in person, while converting every transaction into dollars before the money reaches the county. Fernandez announced the change in a statement on the Tax Collector’s website, calling it a way to give property owners another option without putting public funds into the asset. Payers can select a cryptocurrency option during online checkout or request it at the counter, then connect a supported exchange account or digital wallet and authorize the payment. A third-party system converts the bitcoin into U.S. dollars at the time of payment, the office said, so it never holds, invests in or manages any cryptocurrency. The office said it still receives the full dollar amount owed and records the transactions in its standard payment reports, without county workers maintaining digital wallets. “Government must keep up with the times and the needs of the people we serve,” Fernandez said. “By accepting Bitcoin as a payment option, we are giving property owners another way to pay their taxes, whether online or in person, while continuing to offer the traditional payment methods they already know and trust.” He added that the office is “embracing new technology without compromising our responsibility to protect taxpayer dollars.” Whether someone pays with bitcoin or a conventional method, he said, “our office receives the full amount owed in U.S. dollars.” The office did not name the payment processor or say whether bitcoin payments carry a convenience fee. Card and mobile-wallet payments already carry a nonrefundable 2.50% fee online, with a $2.50 minimum, the office’s payment-methods page shows. Traditional options, including checks, cards, cash and fee-free eChecks, remain available. The announcement covers property taxes, and the option is voluntary. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Hyperscale Data (GPUS) Sells Its Last Bitcoin for AI Data Center, Months After Chasing $100 Million Treasury Hyperscale Data has sold the last of its bitcoin, the NYSE American-listed company said Tuesday, unloading about 211.56 BTC for roughly $16 million to pay down debt and fund an AI data center in Michigan. The sales were completed by Nov. 8 at about $76,000 per coin. Since it first sold part of its reserve in late July, Hyperscale has sold approximately 1,113 bitcoin for about $74.4 million, the company said. That works out to an average of roughly $66,800 per coin. At today’s price near $74,200, the same 1,113 BTC would be worth about $82.6 million. The company, which trades under the ticker GPUS, said the money will go toward its Michigan site, where it aims to energize the first 10 megawatts of critical IT capacity in December. “We believe bringing that capacity online is our quickest path to profitability,” CEO Will Horne said in the release. “Selling our Bitcoin reserves reduces our exposure to Bitcoin price swings and gives us cash to pay down debt and fund the work in Michigan. We believe that’s the best use of this capital for all our stockholders.” From a $100 million target to zero The exit is a sharp reversal from Hyperscale’s plans this summer. In late July, the company reported holding more than 1,106 bitcoin and said it wanted to build a $100 million digital asset treasury and reach full parity between its bitcoin holdings and its market capitalization. “Every Bitcoin we acquire further strengthens Hyperscale Data’s balance sheet and expands our financial flexibility,” Executive Chairman Milton “Todd” Ault III said at the time. “We intend to continue building our Bitcoin position over time.” A week later, Hyperscale disclosed its first sale , about 150.5 BTC, leaving it with roughly 958.5 BTC as of Aug. 2, even as its Ault Capital Group subsidiary bought about 15 BTC on the open market. The holdings were split between that unit and Sentinum. Ault said then that the company planned to keep a long-term position while tapping it for short-term flexibility, adding, “We are confident in our ability to use Bitcoin as pristine collateral.” Tuesday’s release closes that chapter. Hyperscale said it still mines bitcoin at its Montana site and expects any bitcoin it holds on its balance sheet going forward to come “primarily” from its own mining operations. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Down Near $73,500 After Hot CPI Print Lifts Fed Hike Bets Bitcoin price traded near $73,500 on Tuesday morning, down about 1% over the past day and roughly $32,000 below its price one year ago, after a hotter-than-expected inflation report revived fears of a larger Federal Reserve rate hike, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The U.S. consumer price index rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists expected. Core CPI, which strips out food and energy, climbed 0.3% against forecasts for 0.2%. Bitcoin price had been holding near $74,300 in the minutes before the 8:30 a.m. ET release. Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no yield, and that math has capped the bitcoin price since Friday’s strong jobs report. Bitcoin had already been soft overnight. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. entertainment.description: The Flamingos celebrate on stage with green and white confetti as they lift the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup trophy. History was made in Rabat as the Flamingos of Nigeria conquered global football at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Under head coach Akeem Busari , the team executed an extraordinary seven-match campaign at the finals, overcoming an early setback to claim six consecutive victories and become the first African nation to lift any FIFA women’s international trophy. Midfielder Oluebube Umejiaku earned individual recognition by winning the FIFA Golden Ball as the Player of the Tournament alongside Player of the Match honors in the final. The squad also displayed exceptional attacking breadth, scoring goals through eight different players across seven matches at the finals while registering over 100 goal attempts. Oluebube Umejiaku poses with the FIFA Golden Ball and Player of the Match awards following Nigeria’s World Cup triumph. Here is the match-by-match breakdown of how Nigeria navigated the African qualifiers, powered through the World Cup group stage, defeated multi-time global champions in the knockouts, and clinched the ultimate trophy in Morocco. Nigeria’s Flamingos celebrate becoming the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating Japan 2-1 in Rabat. Phase 1: The African Qualifying Journey Nigeria entered the African U-17 World Cup qualifying campaign in the second round, establishing dominance in home-and-away aggregate ties across West Africa. The Flamingos opened their qualification run with an emphatic 5–0 away victory in Guinea, led by team captain Harmony Chidi ’s first-half hat-trick alongside goals from Oluwakemi Adegbuyi and Mary Dunstan . They followed up with a 7–0 victory in the home leg in Ogun State to complete a 12–0 aggregate shutout. The Flamingos celebrate on the pitch following their matchday four fixture at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. In the final qualifying round, Nigeria established a three-goal lead in Monrovia by defeating Liberia 4–1, thanks to a brace from Harmony Chidi and goals from Shakirat Moshood and Peace Effiong . Chidi then sealed a 2–0 second-leg win back home to finish the qualifiers with 12 goals and secure Nigeria’s ticket to Morocco. Phase 2: Group B at the World Cup (Morocco) Placed in Group B alongside Poland, Puerto Rico, and defending world champions DPR Korea, Nigeria had to battle through one of the tournament’s most competitive pools. The campaign started with a tight 2–1 loss to Poland in Rabat, putting pressure on the team to perform in their remaining fixtures. The Flamingos bounced back immediately with a 2–0 shutout victory over Puerto Rico to claim their first three points. Nigeria’s Flamingos celebrate their historic 3-1 Group B victory over defending champions DPR Korea in Morocco. In their final group match, Nigeria produced one of the tournament’s biggest tactical upsets by defeating two-time defending champions DPR Korea

sports.description: Simsbury football coach Jim Caouette talks with Hunter Woolf during a 27-7 win over Newington at Holden Field in Simsbury on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. (Bryant Carpenter/Hearst Connecticut Media) SIMSBURY - The leaves are off the trees beyond the north end zone of Holden Field, but the Simsbury Trojans who play there remain at peak. With a 27-7 win over Newington on Friday night, Simsbury football improved to 7-1. Which means the town that is home to the Pinchot Sycamore, the state's biggest tree, is home to the team enjoying the season's biggest turnaround in Connecticut high school football . Mark the rings on the trunk: Simsbury was 1-9 a year ago, 2-8 in 2024 and 1-9 in 2023. Heading into 2026, the team had its third head coach in as many years come through the door. He's proven to be a good one. Jim Caouette, the longtime defensive coordinator at Holy Cross-Waterbury and one-time head coach at Avon, a ball of energy and new schemes on both sides of the ball, harnessed a 19-strong group of seniors hungry to win as they once did before they got to high school. Another advantage: Simsbury moved down a rung on the Central Connecticut Conference ladder, from Tier 2 to Tier 3. There, the Trojans have not lost since dropping their season opener to Middletown, 40-35. They've won seven straight, the second-longest streak in program history, and stand No. 4 in the CIAC Class L playoff rankings. They are on course to match the 9-1 of 2019, the last time Simsbury football reached the postseason. It had been one long dry spell since, a meager 12 wins across five seasons. This fall, the Trojans pushed all that to the curb. "I think last year and years prior we've just been beating ourselves up on our own; it's been 'Simsbury versus Simsbury' is what the coaches say," remarked senior captain and lineman Brett Osborne. "So I think we've really learned how to take it in and move forward instead of taking steps backwards." The Trojans have two games remaining with E.O. Smith and Glastonbury. Their plus-6 shift in victories so far puts them ahead of several other teams of marked improvement this season. Lewis Mills/Wolcott Tech (2-8 to 6-2), New Milford (1-9 to 5-3) and the SMSA Co-op (1-9 to 5-2) each improved by four wins thus far. Of note: New London and Thames River are also under new coaching regimes. Jack Cochran is back at New London after being out of the game for 13 years. He is better known as the assistant coach who oversaw the Holy Cross defense for the next decade while his son Drew became the school's top all-time passer . sports.title: Stephen Jones Admits Dallas Must Learn To Close Games Now
sports.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys barely survived a close battle with the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, but the victory does not mean the job is done. Stephen Jones, the team’s co-owner, made it clear that the franchise still has a key lesson to learn after the 27-23 win. The game felt eerily similar to the loss against Arizona the week before, and the team needs to fix its habit of letting leads slip away. Jones did not mince words about the state of the squad. “I think it’s something that — it’s a learning experience. I still think we’ve got a long ways to go,” Jones said. The team has to learn how to win and how to close out games, which remains a major problem for this group. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer agrees with this assessment and knows the team must do better things to succeed. Penalties Are Killing Dallas The most glaring issue on the field was a lack of discipline that nearly cost the Cowboys the game. Pro Football Network reported that Dallas’s 14 penalties totaling 153 yards erased over 100 yards of total offense. Former NFL star Chad Johnson was furious about the sloppy play and warned the team that they cannot have so many penalties if they want to win. Johnson compared the team’s behavior to the Oakland Raiders of the 80s and 90s. The worst moment came when inactive linebacker DeMarvion Overshown ran onto the field in street clothes to celebrate a big play. Referee Clay Martin called an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for the non-uniform player in blue sweats and a stocking cap. “After the play, unsportsmanlike conduct by Dallas. We had a non-uniform player in blue sweats and a stocking cap come onto the field to celebrate. That’s a 15-yard penalty,” the official announced. After a mistake shifted Dallas from its own 33-yard line to the 18, Indianapolis tied the game following a three-and-out. Closing The Game Remains A Struggle Even with a strong offensive showing, the Cowboys could not put the game away when they had the chance. Quarterback Dak Prescott called the offensive penalties “purely unacceptable” after the game, highlighting the frustration within the locker room. The team has made good plays, but drives often end up the way no one wants them to end in terms of moving the ball and scoring. “In this particular case, last week was no different closing the game out. We’re just not getting that done right now,” Jones noted regarding the struggles to finish drives. The Cowboys now sit at a 4-5 record on the season and must clean up these mistakes quickly. With the playoff race still alive, the team trails the New York Giants by just 2.5 games for first place in the NFC East. Dallas faces a tough test next as they prepare to play the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 4:25 p.m. ET at AT&T Stadium.

sports.title: Real Madrid midfielder set to undergo tests after suffering injury in national team camp
sports.description: Real Madrid midfielder set to undergo tests after suffering injury in national team camp The international break has just begun but it appears that disaster has already struck as far as Real Madrid are concerned. One of their key players, Aurelien Tchouameni has suffered an injury while away with the France national team, reports L’Equipe . Tchouameni injured again Tchouameni missed the start of the 2026/27 season due to an injury he had sustained with France at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. While he returned to action in September, new France manager Zinedine Zidane opted not to call him up to the squad during the previous international break, giving him time to fully recover his fitness and rhythm. Injured again? (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Since then, Tchouameni has done exactly that, once again establishing himself as an important player for Los Blancos , and earning a recall to the French national team for their upcoming UEFA Nations League matches against Italy and Turkiye. However, as per the report, Tchouameni was forced to stop training during today’s session after suffering a groin injury. Having been unable to complete the session, the 26-year-old midfielder will now undergo tests to determine the nature and severity of the injury. Once that is done, it will be decided whether Tchouameni will travel to Italy with the rest of the France squad return to the club. Concern for Real Madrid As already mentioned, Tchouameni has once again become an integral part of the Real Madrid setup under Jose Mourinho. A key cog in Mourinho’s system. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The French midfielder is key to providing the defensive solidity on the field operating alongside someone like Bernardo Silva in the double pivot. Since returning from injury, he has made ten appearances for Real Madrid in all competitions, starting eight of those, indicating the faith that Mourinho has in him. As such, if Tchouameni is injured with the France national team camp, it will come as a big blow for Los Blancos heading into an important stretch of the season. For now, those at Valdebebas will be eagerly awaiting results of the French international’s medical examinations and hoping that the groin issue he is dealing with does not turn out to be something serious.

sports.description: For the Wolverines, there were plenty of takeaways from their first loss of the season. If they want to beat the top teams in the country, they can’t shoot 25% from 3-point range. They can’t commit 27 fouls and give the opponent 36 free-throw attempts. They can’t have starting guard Trey McKenney go scoreless for an entire half. And they can’t have the entire bench combine for just eight points on 2-for-12 shooting like it did in the 85-77 setback against UConn in Boston. “I don't think we have somebody we think can come in and just — like Trey came off the bench last year, he was a scorer. L.J. Cason came off the bench last year. We knew we were going to get points from those guys,” Michigan coach Mike Boynton Jr. said. “I think this year it’s still kind of a wait and see because we don't have a bunch of guys who've done it so far.” One of the many things that made last season’s national title team so great was its reliable depth. Michigan had multiple reserves who could score in double figures on any given night. Whenever the Wolverines went to their bench, there wasn’t much drop-off and the second unit often helped create separation on the scoreboard. Two of those key pieces — guard Roddy Gayle Jr. and McKenney — have moved into the starting lineup this season. Who is going to replace what they brought off the bench? Who is going to be the playmaker that provides instant offense like Cason did? Who is going to create a spark with energy and effort like Will Tschetter did? That’s what Michigan is in the process of figuring out as the roles are being defined during the early stages of the season. Of course, losing star freshman Brandon McCoy Jr. to a torn ACL was a massive blow. sports.description: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks at the scoreboard during the second quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2 p.m. MT, and our Denver Broncos could be an active team prior to the deadline. They have been widely connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor in the days leading up to the deadline , but according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the team could explore adding a weapon or two to their offense. He mentions running back, tight end, and wide receiver as the positions that they could add. With Harvey injury and Badie also on IR and injuries across the offense, would expect Broncos to explore adding a weapon or two before trade deadline (RB, TE, WR). https://t.co/TSad3tJ2d3 — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) October 31, 2026 Looking at the Broncos’ needs heading into the deadline, the most glaring one is running back. Now, the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman helps, but the Broncos still need more from the position. RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie are on the injured reserve, and veteran JK Dobbins has been struggling all season. So, adding another back to pair with Coleman would make sense. The question is, will they go big and add a Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall? Or make a smaller move for someone like Tony Pollard or someone else? Klis mentions wide receiver, and while it may not be the most pressing need right now, it could be in a few months. Jaylen Waddle has not performed as expected thus far; Courtland Sutton will be 32 next season and has a large cap hit(Also restructured his deal and could be off the team next season); Pat Bryant has been very good, but has been on the IR; Marvin Mims is a pending free agent, while Troy Franklin is buried on the depth chart. Could the Broncos be looking to add a wide receiver who could contribute to this team this season and moving forward? This doesn’t seem as likely, but I wouldn’t rule it out if the right deal comes their way. As for tight end, I don’t know. The only name that could move the needle and that might be available is Dallas Goedert, but is that even worth it? He would certainly improve that room, but the Broncos really do not utilize their tight ends in the passing game. Evan Engram has had a disappointing year, and blocking specialist Nate Adkins leads the group (and, funny enough, the team) in TD receptions with 3, but he only has 6 total catches thus far. sports.title: Virgil Van Dijk “Not in Any Panic” About Contract Situation
sports.description: With Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk turning 35 just ahead of the start of the 2026-27 season and now into the final year of his contract, questions about what the future might hold for the Premier League legend have of late begun to push their way into the conversation. For Van Dijk, though, the focus remains on the present. Or at least that’s what he’s telling anyone who asks, with the Dutch international—who pulled out of his country’s latest round of friendlies and will miss national team duty for the first time since 2020—being pressed on the issue this week. “I feel good, but it’s not about me at the moment,” he said when asked if he sees himself continuing at the highest levels, and at Liverpool in particular, beyond the current campaign. “Let’s see, but I’m not in any panic. I want to keep playing and to continue what I’m doing. “So let’s see what the season brings, but I’ve had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, then that’s the case. If not, then I will have to go somewhere else. There’s nothing to report at the moment but that doesn’t mean that there’s any stress about it or anything.” While Liverpool look to have gotten back on track under new manager Andoni Iraola, they probably aren’t quite at the stage yet where they could be counted as title contenders—and if that’s going to take another year, we’ll be hoping Van Dijk is around to take part in another title race. And in the meantime, too, even if the Reds are currently nine points back of Arsenal, there are other prizes they will expect to seriously push for this season—from the League Cup and FA Cup to the Champions League—and Van Dijk remains key to any success they do have.

technology.title: 14-year-old creates tool for AI agents to band together like a team
technology.description: Built by a 14-year-old developer, a new tool called Autark treats AI agents as a virtual team that can work without constant prompting. Users put tasks in an inbox, where a manager agent delegates them to other agents that carry out the work and report their results. Agents can also ask clarifying questions if tasks are too vague. “Agents do not wait for a prompt,” Autark’s website explains . “A schedule, a timer, a new task, a message or an event wakes them up. They decide what to do, do it, and can plan their own next step.” As one would hope from a product like this, Autark is model agnostic and can be set up to connect to OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, and Kimi Code through those services’ CLI tools. Local models are also supported. Your mileage may vary if you choose to use anything besides Codex or Claude Code, though, as Autark’s website mentions support for other models is built in but hasn’t been tested in a live run yet, as Autark is still under active development as an open-source tool. Real teenage engineering Autark is the brainchild of teenage Austrian developer Stanislaus Hees. He’s still in school, and tells The Register he’s deeply interested in AI and came up with Autark after being unhappy with existing AI tools. “I could get help with individual tasks, but I still had to organise the work, remember what was unfinished and keep pushing it forward,” Hees said of his time using Claude Code and Codex. “I wanted a system that could take responsibility for ongoing work, not just respond to my next message.” He developed Autark - or, more accurately, prompted AI coding tools to do it for him - to come up with a tool that could fulfill that want. It doesn’t stop agents from spending all the money they can get their hands on, deleting files, or sending unsolicited emails, either. Agents run with the privileges of the machine's user, with approval checks and permission restrictions disabled or bypassed. We asked Thunderbird when we can expect to see Thundermail officially launched and open to all comers. We will update if we get an answer. It previously said that a full launch is expected sometime in 2026. technology.title: AMD winds up Zen 6 cores for faster clock speeds
technology.description: After teasing its 256-core Epycs for more than a year, AMD is finally ready to talk about architectural changes to the Zen core that not only make it possible, but will eventually power its next generation of Ryzen processors in desktop and mobile PCs. During a press event in Las Vegas last week, AMD spilled the beans on its latest Zen cores, which promise an average 27 percent uplift in instructions per clock (IPC) across a variety of AI and server workloads, along with boosted clocks ranging from 4.1 to 5.3 GHz. We expect to see even higher frequencies on consumer chips before long, but AMD isn’t quite ready to talk about Ryzen just yet. CPU performance is a function of power, IPC, and clocks, and with gains across all three, the cores are shaping up to be one of the company’s biggest generational jumps ever. A tale of two cores As in past Epyc launches, Zen 6 isn’t one core. It comes in two flavors: a frequency-optimized variant (Zen 6) and a density-optimized version (Zen 6c). This split dates back to the launch of AMD’s Bergamo Epycs in 2023, which packed 128 compact Zen 4c cores into just eight chiplets. The chip’s debut drew comparisons to Intel’s still relatively new Efficient (E-cores) for obvious reasons. But under the hood, AMD’s Zen 4c was nothing like what Intel was doing. The core itself was nearly identical to Zen 4; it simply traded clocks and a bit of cache per core for a more densely packed CPU die. The only difference between running an application on Bergamo or Genoa was how quickly it executed. The same could not be said of Intel’s P and E cores, which used different ISAs. This remained a defining characteristic and advantage of AMD’s compact core architecture through Zen 5, which allowed it to ship Turin parts with up to 192 cores without users having to worry about whether their app was running on a compact core or not. With Zen 6c, at least as we understand it, this philosophy is largely unchanged. Both Zen 6 and Zen 6c share the same ISA, with clock being the main differentiator. There are other micro-architectural differences between the two cores designed to balance IPC and clock speeds more effectively. Looking at the core’s block diagram, this isn’t immediately obvious. Zen 6 and Zen 5 share a very similar front and backend. We'd be tempted to call the core iterative if it weren't for the 20 to 31 percent IPC uplift for cloud and AI workloads that AMD claims over Zen 5. This suggests that core for core, a 4.1 GHz Zen 6c-based Venice Epyc should deliver performance on par with a Zen 5-based Turin Epyc running at 5 GHz. That's a pretty sizable jump, but just because AMD is seeing generational performance uplift in enterprise server and cloud workloads doesn't mean we'll see the same gains on the client side. science.title: Uranus has a weird magnetic field that's stumped scientists for 40 years — we may finally know why
science.description: The posided magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune may stem from extreme conditions lying within their deep interior. Unravelling the mystery behind the magnetic fields of these worlds is giving us new insight into the little-known interiors of the ice giants. Only one spacecraft has ever visited Uranus and Neptune, the Voyager 2 spacecraft which spend past Uranus in January 1986 and Neptune in August 1989. Voyager 2 found that their planetary magnetic fields were, to put it bluntly, wonky. Uranus’ magnetic field was offset from its rotational axis by 59 degrees and isn’t even centered on the planet’s core, but instead is only two-thirds of the way down. Neptune is similar, with a disordered magnetic field offset by 47 degrees and centered halfway between the core and its visible cloud tops. If we compare these planets to Earth , which has a stable magnetic field tilted by just 11 degrees to our planet’s rotation, we can see how extreme the magnetic fields of the ice giants are. Various explanations for the strange magnetic fields of the ice giants have been put forward over the years. Uranus as a whole is tilted by 97 degrees and effectively rolls around the sun , and speculation is that billions of years ago it was knocked on its side by a collision with a long-lost Earth-sized planet. Could this collision have also skewed its magnetic field? This might be a plausible explanation were Neptune’s magnetic field also not similarly skewed without having experienced a collision. Clearly, whatever the cause, it must be intrinsic to the nature of the two ice giant planets. Now, a new study by scientists in the U.S. and the UK, based on computer simulations and Voyager 2’s measurements of the two planets’ magnetic fields, may have found a solution. The solution to the weird magnetic fields of the solar system's ice giants may come down to how planets generate their magnetic field through the dynamo effect. This arises from the swirling, convective motion of an electrically conducting liquid within a rotating body, which is able to generate and maintain a powerful magnetic field. Inside Earth, the electrically conducting fluid is the molten iron in the outer part of our planet’s core, and the magnetic field that it generates has clear north and south poles – what we call a dipole, a phenomenon that we can also see in the two magnetic poles of a simple bar magnet. However, the conditions inside Uranus and Neptune are somewhat different. As ice giants, they contain a lot of volatiles – ammonia, hydrogen, helium, methane, and water surrounding a probable rocky core. Furthermore, Uranus and Neptune are substantially larger than Earth , with 14.5 and 17 times the mass of our planet, respectively. This increased mass creates crushing conditions within the interior of the ice giants. Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

In the final weeks of 1960, two young radio enthusiasts were monitoring transmissions from a home-built listening station on a rooftop in Turin, Italy, when the brothers detected something extraordinary: a faint signal that bore the hallmarks of one originating from space. That wasn't the only surprising thing about the alleged signal:, the transmission carried a very familiar message: it was Morse code for the international distress signal SOS. As the youths listened, the signal seemed to grow weaker. This raised a troubling possibility: could it be that the signal's source was moving farther away from Earth ? And if so, was it possible that this concerning signal was of Soviet origin — perhaps a spacecraft drifting helplessly into space, carrying a cosmonaut on board whose doomed mission had never been publicly acknowledged? These strange events from November 1960 became the first in a series of alleged radio signal interceptions that would form the basis of an enduring Cold War-era mystery involving so-called "lost cosmonauts" — early Soviet space travelers rumored to have died during secret spaceflight missions before Yuri Gagarin's historic flight the following spring, in April 1961.Today, more than six decades later, the story remains one of the most haunting legends of the Space Age. Were there truly early Soviet space missions — with tragically ill-fated cosmonaut crews — that remain undisclosed to this day? science.description: 5 min read NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets — worlds beyond our solar system — throughout our galaxy. Watch to learn how the presence of a planet modifies the gravitational wave signal from tightly orbiting white dwarfs. The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory could detect a Jupiter-mass planet in such systems up to thousands of light-years away. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center Download high-resolution video from NASA’s Scientific Visualization Studio “The most common source for LISA is expected to be double white dwarf systems, which are binaries composed of white dwarfs in tight orbits,” said Casey McGrath, a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County and NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland. “If an exoplanet also orbits within one of these systems, its presence becomes imprinted on the gravitational wave signal in a way we’ll be able to uncover.” Two papers published Tuesday in The Astrophysical Journal detail the findings. The first , authored solely by McGrath, examines the detection method and determines the planet masses and orbital periods where it would work best. The second paper , by McGrath and coauthors, investigates how such planets could be confirmed using NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope . The possibility of detecting exoplanets around LISA double white dwarf systems was first proposed by Japanese astronomer Naoki Seto in 2008. Led by ESA (European Space Agency), the LISA mission is slated for launch in the mid-2030s. As a collaborative partner, NASA is contributing the telescopes, other critical hardware, and engineering and scientific support as part of its mission to better understand how the universe works. The LISA detection method is similar to one called radial velocity that uses light and is already employed to find exoplanets around nearby stars. As a planet orbits, its gravity tugs on its host star, imparting a small reflex motion, or wobble, onto it. This wobble causes the star’s spectrum to oscillate, with spectral lines shifting from redder wavelengths as the star moves away from us to bluer ones as the star moves toward us. The DARPA-funded project saw a robotic "truss builder" create a reflective antenna using Kapton film, composite fiber tubes and aluminum joints. The implications are huge for future missions, potentially opening up new possibilities to build — or fix — satellites in the final frontier. "This is the first time that a structure has been autonomously constructed in space ," Sergio Pellegrino, an aerospace and civil engineering professor at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), said in a statement on Nov. 5 . The need for such spacecraft will likely rise substantially in the future, as companies assemble giant megaconstellations for cell-phone communications, AI compute and other purposes. Indeed, the ball is already rolling on such ambitious projects, generating enough hype for space startups around the globe to raise a record $20.8 billion in the third quarter of 2026 alone. Anything that launches aboard a rocket is limited by the size of that vehicle's fairing — the nose cone that protects payloads during their ride to space. In space, however, the ability to stretch out is practically infinite — after taking into account, of course, engineering and financing constraints. Assembling structures robotically off Earth could therefore be revolutionary, advocates say. And the recent milestone was a step in that direction. "This work could be useful not only for astronomy and astrophysics, but also for communications and other areas, such as building very large solar arrays for space solar power ," said Pellegrino, who's team leader of the truss-building project, a Caltech demonstration mission called Autonomous In-Space Tensioned Reflector Assembly (ASTRA). It uses an onboard focusing process to make a composite of images of the same target acquired at different positions to focus on multiple features in a single image. Why is it incredible? Scientists theorize that the "discs and needles" texture takes its characteristic shape as crystals, or "crystal forms," grow. The relatively large sizes of the crystal forms at "Nazca" may provide clues about the temperatures at which they grew, as well as information about the abundance of salts and fluids in the area at the time. Complicating this picture, however, is the fact that mineral crystals can be replaced by other minerals after their original crystallization. The new minerals are known as "pseudomorphs," because they have the same shape as the original minerals but not the same composition or molecular structure. The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of Nazca — which shares its name with an ancient South American civilization that's famous for the large designs it etched into the rock and dirt — before drilling begins. The NASA researchers will then be able to compare the deeper composition to the surface-level composition.

science.title: What is the electrification target at COP31 and can countries meet it?
science.description: Relying on electricity for more of our energy is vital to efforts to limit global warming Christian Hütter/mauritius images GmbH/Alamy One of the key items being discussed at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, this week is a voluntary global target to increase electricity’s share of total final energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035. This 35 by 35 target is based on analysis by the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) on what is needed to keep the 1.5°C global warming target within reach. Currently, electricity is estimated to make up just 23.4 per cent of the energy delivered to consumers, known as final energy – a figure that has increased by only 6.7 percentage points since 2000. This means that hitting the target will require the rate of electrification to quadruple compared with the first quarter of the 21st century and triple compared with the rate between 2020 and 2025. Judit Hecke at New Climate Institute, a German think tank, says such an acceleration is possible but “the challenge is getting policies, investment and infrastructure moving at the same pace”. Advertisement Progress on renewable energy has been encouraging, with renewables making up a higher proportion of overall electricity production year after year, and renewable capacity additions have been setting new records each year. In 2024, the most recent IRENA data, nearly 32 per cent of global electricity production came from renewable sources compared with just 18 per cent in 2000. Renewable energy capacity has increased from 0.8 terawatts in 2000 to 5.2 terawatts in 2025. But this is a long way from the COP28 pledge for UN member states to reach 11 terawatts of renewable capacity by 2030. However, Hecke points out that the electrification target includes electricity regardless of how it is generated, meaning that a country could make progress while still heavily relying on coal and gas in the power sector. Electrification, renewables and energy efficiency should be looked at together as the “three pillars of the energy transition”, says Hecke. “At COP31, governments should back the target as part of this wider transition and set out how they will deliver it nationally.” Read more Solar energy is going to power the world much sooner than you think Jan Rosenow at the University of Oxford says the 35 by 35 target is “broadly the right level of ambition” and it is achievable now that electric vehicles , electrical industrial heat and heat pumps are often the cheapest options. “Most new electricity generation built today is renewables and batteries. science.title: Total solar eclipse 2027 vs 2028 — Which one should you choose, Egypt or Australia?
science.description: null For those who want to experience a total solar eclipse, the next two years present the best kind of problem. On Aug. 2, 2027, the so-called "eclipse of the century " will sweep across southern Spain, North Africa and the Middle East, bringing more than six minutes of totality to parts of Egypt. Then, on July 22, 2028, another exceptionally long total solar eclipse will cross Australia, putting the remote Outback and Sydney Harbor in the path of the moon's dark central shadow before it reaches New Zealand's beautiful South Island. Both eclipses will be spectacular, and both will require careful planning, yet they promise very different experiences. The 2027 event combines over six minutes of totality with some of the very best weather prospects possible, while 2028 offers over five minutes of totality above some of the world's most famous wildernesses and cityscapes. Eclipse chasing requires careful planning and dedication, but also significant funds. If you can only choose one, which should it be? 2027 total solar eclipse: pros and cons A map of the 2027 total solar eclipse path. (Image credit: Michael Zeiler/EclipseAtlas.com) On paper, 2027 is difficult to beat. Maximum totality on Aug. 2 will last about 6 minutes, 23 seconds, making it the longest totality on land since 1991 and until 2114. The path of totality will cross southern Spain and Gibraltar before sweeping across Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, Sudan, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Somalia and the Chagos Islands. About 88.9 million people live in its path, according to Time and Date . It will dominate the news for weeks. For Europeans, southern Spain is the obvious easy option. Tarifa, at the country's southern tip, will see about 4 minutes, 39 seconds of totality, while the U.K. Overseas Territory of Gibraltar gets about 4 minutes, 25 seconds. Travel farther east and the duration increases, with Sfax in Tunisia getting around 5 minutes, 41 seconds and locations in Egypt experiencing more than six minutes. Weather prospects generally improve, too, as the path crosses the deserts of North Africa. Egypt is the headline destination. Luxor will see about 6 minutes, 20 seconds of totality near midday, with Karnak Temple, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the world's greatest ancient monuments nearby. science.title: NASA's twin ESCAPADE Mars probes slingshot around Earth in unprecedented double 'gravity assist'
science.description: null Twin NASA spacecraft are wrapping up a year-long escapade, ready to make a beeline to the Red Planet. The Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers (ESCAPADE) spacecraft launched in November 2025 on the second-ever flight of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket. But rather than head straight to Mars, the two spacecraft dawdled through a looping trajectory . Now, they are back in Earth's neighborhood where they tackled a crucial engine burn unusually close to Earth that — if all goes well — will set them on track for Mars . "No NASA mission has ever done this before," said Rob Lillis, a planetary and space physicist at the University of California, Berkeley and principal investigator of the ESCAPADE mission. "For most missions, it just isn't necessary." That's because traditionally NASA's Mars missions have been carefully choreographed within cosmic launch constraints, leaving Earth during a brief window of planetary alignment that only occurs every 26 months. ESCAPADE was meant to launch in October 2024, when Earth and Mars were favorably aligned, but delays with the New Glenn rocket forced the mission to sit out the precious launch window. Rather than wait to launch this fall, NASA decided to try something new. ESCAPADE mission planners designed a "loitering" orbit , shaped like a kidney bean. It called for the twin probes to loop through that trajectory to be back at Earth in early November 2026, ready to continue on to Mars. The ESCAPADE mission's unique path to reach Mars. After launching in November 2025, the twin ESCAPADE probes looped around the Earth-Sun Lagrange point 2 (L2), in a "loiter" orbit that returned them to Earth in November 2026 where they used our planet's gravity to slingshot themselves to Mars. (Image credit: Advanced Space/Matt Bolliger) Once they arrived, however, the twin probes faced a major hurdle: Each had to perfectly execute an engine burn within Earth's gravity well. The maneuver is similar to the slingshot flybys that spacecraft regularly conduct to adjust their trajectories — but here, the probes had to fire their engines to amp up the effect of the burn rather than acting alone. The first spacecraft tackled the feat on Nov. 7; the second did so on Monday (Nov. 9). And according to NASA, the burns went perfectly. science.title: Global carbon emissions set to fall in 2026 due to Iran energy shock
science.description: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz led to a spike in oil prices Anna Ivanova/Alamy Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are expected to drop this year for the first time in five years. The slowdown has been partly attributed to the energy shock triggered by the US and Israel’s war on Iran. The conflict, which began in February, led to a jump in oil prices after the Strait of Hormuz, the main trade route for about 20 per cent of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas, was blockaded by Iran in response. This is still affecting petrol prices and household gas bills, and has seen countries around the world turn to alternative fuel types to boost energy security. Advertisement Read more Solar energy is going to power the world much sooner than you think Around 38.2 gigatonnes of CO2 are expected to be emitted in 2026 globally, according to the latest annual Global Carbon Budget – put together by more than 140 researchers. This is a 0.4 per cent decrease on the previous year, largely due to a projected 1.9 per cent fall in emissions from oil. The drop in oil use was partly offset by a 0.6 per cent increase in emissions from coal. Robbie Andrew at climate research group CICERO in Oslo, Norway, one of the report authors, says financial pressures due to the energy shock are likely to have caused the drop in emissions this year, which may turn out to be a “blip”. “On the assumption that there are no further crises, then you’d expect that emissions would bounce back,” says Andrew. The two biggest dips in emissions in the 21st century have been attributed to the covid-19 pandemic, which saw emissions drop by around 6 per cent in 2020, and the global financial crisis, which saw emissions drop around 2 per cent in 2009. The future outlook depends on how long the energy shock lasts, says Andrew, with governments forced to look at the economic case for continuing to subsidise fossil fuels. The rollout of renewable energy also played a part in bringing down carbon emissions. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power are predicted to offset 64 to 79 per cent of increasing emissions from demand growth through to 2028. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter In China, the world’s biggest emitter of CO2, emissions are projected to decrease by 0.9 per cent in 2026 as the country continues to make strides with expanding renewable energy and electric vehicles. “What’s keeping emissions down is the renewable energy, and the price of oil actually suppresses this even more,” says Corinne Le Quéré at the University of East Anglia, UK, who also worked on the report. “So, that’s encouraging in a way, but it does mean that if the price of oil rebounds to pre-Iran [conflict] levels, most likely the emissions will rebound as well until we have enough further acceleration in renewable energy to really bring the emissions down durably.” Journal Reference: Nature Climate Change DOI: 10.1038/s41558-026-02821-8
